content:
- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods; model tends to overshoot after positive sentiment spikes.
- Underestimate prices during negative sentiment phases; model reacts too slowly to bearish signals.
- Forecast tends to lag behind true price movements, especially in the first 5–7 days of the 30-day horizon.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model often overcorrects downward, missing upward momentum.
- In sustained upward trends, model fails to capture the full magnitude of the rally, especially after a 7–10 day uptick.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overestimates near peaks and underestimates near troughs, especially when sentiment is volatile.
- If sentiment is consistently positive over 3–5 days, model should adjust upward by 2–3% beyond the historical mean to avoid underestimating the trend.
- When sentiment turns negative after a spike, model often fails to anticipate the correction, leading to overestimation of the peak.
